newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: -- Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai ended up across the board on Monday, with turnover rising sharply to 10.2 million lots from 5.30 million last Friday.
The annual rate for the three-day contract surged to 12.15 percent from 4.35 percent and the most active seven-day contract ended up at 11.98 percent from 9.58 percent.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said that, with two issues of domestic A shares on Tuesday and Thursday, liquidity flew out of the repo market, pushing up the rates, especially early-maturing contracts.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down, after sharp gains last week on a bank interest rate cut by the central bank in late August, traders said. Combined market volume fell to 2.12 million lots from 3.62 million.
But the most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometre, closed slightly up at 122.80 yuan from 122.71 yuan partly due to institutional support, they said.

"Some institutions which bought the 10-year bond last week had to push the contract to a higher level to make profits," one trader said. "The bond is likely to continue to rise for the rest of this week." -- Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
